The prototype reports module realpaths/hashes and distribution metadata; it is not a native grading or package-validity gate. title: Research: compare native verifier cancellation across published Harbor versions
body:
Does published Harbor 0.24.0 avoid verifier retry overlap and stop timed-out processes reliably? Subissue of #33. The bounded experiment and preservation are complete; the upgrade comparison is inconclusive.

**Measured baseline:** Harbor 0.6.6’s finite control passed. Both timeout writers remained alive after the final verifier exception: 34 matching PID observations extend to +10.334 seconds. Docker SIGKILL occurred at +10.574 seconds and container destruction at +10.636. Transient holes appeared, but the final saved log had no NULs. Teardown eventually removed the processes; the verifier deadline itself did not stop them.

**Candidate limit:** installed 0.24.0 source matched its wheel, but its finite trial failed before the writer because its egress-sidecar image build needs Buildx, absent from this minimal runner. The timeout case was skipped as declared. No 0.24.0 cancellation outcome or validated upgrade exists. [Results and interpretation](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/52cb13c5/experiments/43-native-harbor-comparison/results.md).

**Fidelity and preservation:** exact #41 writer/test bytes and five-second verifier deadline; same outside observer for both versions. Baseline dependency constraints match; both native source sets (203/369 members) are verified. No package source, biological task or grading repair. Runtime/final HF readback, owned cleanup and inert post-cleanup invocation are verified; 12.08 MB of duplicates removed. [Completion audit](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/52cb13c5/experiments/43-native-harbor-comparison/completion-audit.md).

**Budget/status:** one attempt used 0.099667 / 2 allocated CPU-hours. Zero outstanding CPU reservations/model calls/new capacity or new biological exports. Existing archival reservation remains unreconciled. Keep open for review; #44 moves established validation behavior toward a supported entrypoint. Logs and artifact details are in comments.

title: Research: assess upstream verifier cancellation and retry log fixes
body:
Can upstream Harbor improve verifier cancellation and retry-log integrity without repository-specific repairs? Subissue of #33 following #41. The source-only assessment is complete; keep open for review.

**Finding:** published Harbor 0.24.0 and pinned current main remove 0.6.6’s automatic single-step verifier retry. Ten inspected release runtime modules match the published PyPI wheel exactly. This is a candidate way to avoid #41’s overlapping retry, not evidence of reliable daemon-side cancellation or compatibility with our pipeline.

**Remaining gaps:** the buffered Docker collector still lacks outer-cancellation cleanup; the streamed collector terminates the CLI subprocess and is opt-in. Neither establishes that the process inside the container is stopped. Outer wait_for, lack of an inner verifier exec deadline and fixed per-trial truncating stdout remain. [Call-path comparison and limits](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/6d359949/experiments/42-upstream-cancellation/results.md).

**Evidence:** exact release/main commits, Git blob hashes, published-wheel parity and 25 structural function checks are recorded. Ten selected test modules per revision were inspected; no upstream code/tests/package were installed or executed. The public source/notices snapshot has three anonymously verified HF objects/69 members; 4.96 MB of duplicates were cleaned up. [Receipt](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/6d359949/experiments/42-upstream-cancellation/evidence-receipt.json).

**Budget and next boundary:** zero native CPU reservation, model calls, new capacity or execution spend. No dependency pin, biological task or historical result was changed. A native upgrade comparison remains unmeasured and needs a separately checkpointed/admitted variant within #33’s existing limits. Detailed logs and provenance are in comments.

title: Research: verify verifier cancellation and retry log integrity
body:
Do verifier processes stop when Harbor 0.6.6 times out, and can retries preserve reliable logs? Subissue of #33; the native diagnostic is complete and remains open for review.

**Finding:** the finite control passed. In the timeout case, Harbor retried while the first writer was still alive, with matching PID/start ticks, the same log inode and old/new descriptor offsets of 60,416/0 bytes. Eleven in-container samples measured transient NUL holes (maximum 59,392 bytes). The native trial returned VerifierTimeoutError without a reward. All 203 pinned Harbor source files, fixture inputs and task resource limits were verified.

**Limit:** the final saved log contains zero NULs. The unchanged predeclared conjunction required final NULs and therefore remains false; survival and transient holes are separate post-run component observations. Historical Scanpy causation and biological task validity remain unproven. [Results and limits](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/b5533ced/experiments/41-verifier-cancellation/results.md).

**Preservation:** two prior fixture/adapter preparation failures are recorded separately. All runtime/final HF objects passed anonymous readback, owned resources are empty and the shared public base is preserved. Deleted 6.94 MB of verified duplicate files; pre/post-cleanup invocations left all 14 stage/budget files unchanged. [Completion audit](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/b5533ced/experiments/41-verifier-cancellation/completion-audit.md).

**Budget:** all three managed attempts used 0.137659 of the original one allocated CPU-hour. Zero outstanding CPU reservations, model calls, new paid capacity or biological task exports. Existing archival reservation remains unreconciled. #42 examines upstream fixes next; no additional execution admitted. Detailed evidence is in comments.

title: Research: transfer recorded-bootstrap export replay to Scanpy
body:
The frozen OHIF replay wrapper does not transfer unchanged to Scanpy. This source-bound assessment is complete; no new Scanpy runtime, failure count or scientific score is claimed. Subissue of #33, kept open for review.

**Evidence:** ten existing public objects were freshly downloaded anonymously. The original transcript, all sixteen recorded actions, 353 pinned upstream source files, task file identities and four historical trials were reverified. The native-inline failure and historical replay used the exact same public base-image ID. [Results and limits](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/1b69450e/experiments/40-recorded-bootstrap-transfer/results.md).

**Two transfer differences:** upstream records failed smoke/fresh flags and caches the image; #39 adds hard rejection gates. Scanpy’s retained checks fail with collection errors, so that rejection would be our outer policy, not upstream pr_runtime. Its verifier also activates a Python venv, which the OHIF PATH-specific probe cannot represent unchanged. No gate, original task or command was changed.

**Historical controls:** both nop/oracle trials time out at 300 and 1200 seconds with no reward. The selected test files collect 952 cases; partial logs reach roughly 68%/90% and contain NUL holes. These are not pass rates, proof of a hang, or evidence that more time alone produces valid controls. Raw archives remain unchanged; #41 investigates cancellation/log integrity separately.

**Durability/budget:** four new source/notice objects and all members passed anonymous HF readback; 818,232 redundant local bytes were removed after verification. Zero new remote jobs, CPU allocation/reservations or model calls. Known unchanged failures were not rerun under the epic’s stopping rule. [Completion audit](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/1b69450e/experiments/40-recorded-bootstrap-transfer/completion-audit.md). Detailed provenance and archive paths are in comments.

title: Research: compare clean inline recipes with recorded bootstrap replay
body:
Deterministic replay recovered the environment omitted by the native clean inline export for frozen OHIF #5996. Subissue of #33; the bounded comparison and evidence lifecycle are complete, and this issue remains open for review.

**Result:** all eighteen unchanged recorded actions and native smoke/fresh checks passed on exactly the same public base image used by #37’s missing-pnpm failure. Original controls gave nop 0/oracle 1: 0/26 → 26/26 F2P, all 1189 P2P passed both sides, oracle command exit 0, zero untracked failures. [Task-level results](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/206535c8/experiments/39-recorded-bootstrap/results.md).

**Integrity:** all eight original grading/instruction/oracle assets and original overlay commands were preserved, with the same 1-CPU/6-GiB/300-second task contract. Candidate changes are the explicit local dependency reference and native provenance. Both control images descend from one verified reconstructed dependency, with equal measured environment probes; their image IDs differ. No command repairs, additional install steps, regeneration or model calls.

**Durability:** anonymous cold input readback preceded compilation; all thirteen runtime HF objects and the final three-object/74-member summary/source snapshot are verified. Real watcher recovery and completed reinvocation passed. Owned remote resources were removed, and 2,172,322 redundant local bytes were deleted after preservation. [Completion audit](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/206535c8/experiments/39-recorded-bootstrap/completion-audit.md).

**Acceptance-policy clarification:** the original check implementations are reused, but this outer wrapper hard-stops on failed smoke/fresh flags whereas upstream caches flagged images. Both checks passed in the OHIF run, so its result is unchanged. [Source note](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/d894c9c2/experiments/39-recorded-bootstrap/analysis/acceptance-policy-note.md).

**Limits and cost:** this is one existing-task attempt, requiring an explicit initializer. The task Dockerfile alone is not standalone; no installed image was published. Future third-party dependency availability and cross-repository reliability remain unproven. One terminal attempt used 0.510124 allocated CPU-hours, zero model calls/new capacity; the unused cleanup reservation was released. #40 assessed unchanged transfer to Scanpy. Detailed provenance and artifact locations are in comments.

title: Research: automate frozen-export validation from a single manifest
body:
Can one manifest-driven controller validate the frozen public exports without per-repository Codex edits, while preserving original grading and explicit failures? Subissue of #33.

**Result:** the resumed frozen controller completed both native families through all eight lifecycle stages. Cobrapy ran 24 controls: all 12 original nop/oracle pairs were positive and all tracked P2P passed on both sides. Only #1482 and #1497 had clean full oracle commands; the other ten exit 1 with additional untracked failures. Scanpy stopped at common build exit 100 before controls because apt could not locate required packages. The 12 OHIF lookup candidates remain unattempted under #37’s sealed shared-prerequisite stop, not twelve measured failures. [Task-level results and limitations](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/fc8f900f/experiments/38-manifest-validation/results.md).

**Automation evidence:** identical worker code and data-only descriptors served both native families. A real watcher restart resumed the same Cobrapy handle; terminal accounting shows one attempt per family. Completed reinvocation returned complete with journals, submissions, accounts, receipts and budget byte-identical. Both raw archives have verified anonymous HF readback and primary cleanup verified empty; Scanpy submission followed Cobrapy’s archive/cleanup. The first local receipt-schema failure occurred before submission and is preserved separately. [Exact evidence](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/tree/fc8f900f/experiments/38-manifest-validation/runs).

**Boundaries:** unchanged native preparation, task recipes, grading, one CPU, 6 GiB and 300-second verifier; no installation/test/targeting repairs, regeneration, models or new capacity. Native positive reward and clean whole-command success remain distinct. Original cohort totals stay 83 exports / 82 ever-positive / 67 ever-clean; these are new attempts, not new unique tasks. Offline failure checks do not imply every emergency path was exercised live. This is frozen-export research validation, not generation yield or production readiness.

**Budget/status:** 0.832063333 allocated CPU-hours for two existing reserved jobs; both emergency reservations released unused. No outstanding CPU reservation, new model calls or recorded paid model cost. The existing archival reservation remains unreconciled. Final summary/source metadata is archived with three verified objects and 49 archive members. Removed 16.2 MB of redundant local inputs after hash-gated readback; immutable payloads and canonical snapshots remain bounded for review/reinvocation. [Acceptance and retention audit](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/998d7f06/experiments/38-manifest-validation/completion-audit.md). #39 investigates recorded-bootstrap fidelity separately. Keep open for review; detailed logs in comments.

title: Research: validate an OHIF inline recipe on a different worker
body:
Does an OHIF inline export rebuild on a different worker with the original controls? Subissue of #33, following #36’s metadata-only cache lookup result.

**Result:** the exact OHIF #5996 candidate failed its first native image build: `pnpm: not found`, exit 127, before Harbor setup, verifier or controls. No repair, repeated build, task score or new control pair. Actual worker differed from original/prior comparison workers, all original images were absent, and all ten task files/eight original grading assets remained unchanged. [Verified result](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/d411058e/experiments/37-ohif-inline-runtime/runtime-readback.json).

**Cause:** original bootstrap reconstruction records Node, Corepack/pnpm and PATH setup; its two reported `rebuild_cmds` omit those persisted steps. Native inline generation renders only the latter, using reconstruction solely for the base `FROM`. The archived committed-image verification therefore does not establish a working clean inline recipe. This failure is independent of the 300-second verifier timeout and PR tests. [Diagnosis and limits](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/d411058e/experiments/37-ohif-inline-runtime/diagnosis.md).

The failing bootstrap prefix is byte-identical across all twelve OHIF candidates; only #5996 was executed. The other eleven runtime outcomes remain unmeasured. This is separate from #36’s fixed metadata lookup and from native registry distribution, which remains untested.

**Preservation/budget:** all 20 HF objects verified anonymously, including raw logs, original bootstrap provenance, exact candidate and source notices. Owned containers/images/volume removed; emergency cleanup released unused. [Archive and cleanup](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/bb4f648a/experiments/37-ohif-inline-runtime/completion-status.json). Used 0.069496 allocated CPU-hours; no models/new capacity. Keep open for review; detailed logs are in comments.

title: Research: resolve native inline recipe cache identity consistently
body:
Can a generic recipe-cache identity change unblock native inline preparation without regenerating tasks or repairing individual environments? Subissue of #33, discovered in #35.

**Result:** the lookup-only experimental candidate prepared all 12 previously blocked OHIF exports. Original pinned upstream preparation failed without changing files. The candidate changes only native Dockerfile/distribution metadata: all 96 original instruction/oracle/grading assets and parsed grading/resource/timeout contracts remain unchanged. [Comparison](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/8fb2a8c9/experiments/36-inline-cache-identity/metadata-comparison.json).

**Cause and candidate:** bootstrap cache paths preserve repository spelling while image tags and reader lookup lowercase it. Current upstream 0.9.4 has the same relevant function bodies as the pinned baseline. The candidate matches cache repository names consistently, validates metadata and rejects ambiguous matching recipes, reusing upstream rendering unchanged. Ten function-level fixtures pass, covering default/legacy/custom roots, missing or conflicting metadata and option-hashed ambiguity. [Protocol](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/c6d939c5/experiments/36-inline-cache-identity/protocol.md).

**Evidence and limits:** all ten HF objects verified anonymously, including 120 candidate task files, source references and notices. Disposable working copies removed. [Archive/cleanup receipt](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/160caec0/experiments/36-inline-cache-identity/completion-status.json). This is an explicit experimental reader replacement, not an unchanged official pipeline result. Candidate images and controls remain untested; no production promotion or upstream contribution is claimed.

**Budget:** zero model calls, Docker operations, remote allocation or new capacity. Archival uses #33’s existing allowance. Keep open for review; detailed logs are in comments. A later runtime test requires its own frozen protocol and resource admission.

title: Research: preserve runnable pr_runtime bundles after worker cleanup
body:
Can a generated task reproduce its controls on a different worker after the original Docker state is removed? Subissue of #33.

**Result:** Cobrapy PR #1482 reproduced its original controls on a different reserved TRC worker using unmodified upstream inline preparation. All four original image references were absent. Nop 0/oracle 1; two F2P repaired, all 17 P2P preserved, oracle exit 0. Eight original instruction/grading/oracle assets and the 300-second verifier/network contract remained unchanged. [Verified runtime evidence](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/c9edb645/experiments/35-durable-runtime-artifacts/cold-summary.json).

All 18 HF snapshot objects have verified anonymous readback, including original logs, native task, provenance, source notices and the preserved analysis correction. Owned containers, images and volumes are removed. [Archive and cleanup receipt](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/8b8a0cca/experiments/35-durable-runtime-artifacts/completion-status.json).

**Coverage and limits:** native metadata preparation succeeded for 13 of 25 eligible public exports; 12 OHIF exports failed cache-name resolution, now tracked in #36. The 58 Matchms exports remain excluded. One task was tested at runtime; this is not cohort-wide portability, image byte identity or registry validation. Two rebuilt image IDs differ; actual source and dependency identities matched both controls. The separate MACS diagnostic’s bare-image-reference limitation remains explicit. No per-task repairs, regeneration or new model calls.

**Budget:** 0.286 allocated CPU-hours used; unused emergency cleanup released. No new capacity or model cost. Evidence uses the epic’s existing archival allowance. Keep open for review; detailed logs are in comments.

title: Research: prepare historical rebuild dependencies without opening task egress
body:
Can base-declared dependency artifacts make a historical PR rebuild work under the exported network guard, without supplying the target project’s published fix? Subissue of #33, following #31.

**Result:** yes for the frozen MACS PR742 compiled-Python diagnostic. The compiled fixture and two real offline-cache comparisons passed. The unattended confirmation recorded nop 0/oracle 1, one F2P repaired, ten P2P preserved, oracle exit 0 and twelve unchanged candidate files. Both builds have identical, source-bound receipts for Cython 3.3.0, NumPy 2.5.4 and setuptools 84.2.1, tied to their respective control intervals. [Diagnosis](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/0eb1bb9b/experiments/34-offline-rebuild/confirmation-diagnosis.md) · [Audited result](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/8628f2c9/experiments/33-unattended-validation/confirmation-summary.json).

The general adaptation prepares binary wheels from the exact base pyproject declarations in a trusted build step, excludes the target distribution, then preserves build isolation and the runtime egress guard. Original instructions, patch, verifier, test assets, commands and 300-second timeout are retained. The first comparison lacked its wheel receipt; that original result remains preserved. The separate confirmation captured receipts before task teardown and exercised the full controller lifecycle, including real interruption/restart and idempotent completion.

All execution and cleanup evidence has verified HF readback. No owned images, containers, controllers, volumes or active controller remain. Total allocation is 4.430 CPU-hours within the twelve-hour child ceiling; all CPU reservations are reconciled. Zero model calls or new capacity. All incremental spending shares #33’s $90 operating ceiling, with storage still reserved rather than billed.

**Limits and next step:** this is one diagnostic task outside the frozen 83-export cohort, with repeated attempts rather than additional unique tasks. Mutable bootstrap inputs and future wheel availability remain limitations. No Docker image bytes are distributed, so clean-worker portability is still #35’s question. No solver score, dataset release or production readiness is claimed. Keep this issue open for review; details and artifacts belong in comments.

title: Epic: make pr_runtime validation unattended and reproducible
body:
**Ready for review:** draft PR #63 provides a manifest-driven official Repo2RLEnv workflow: frozen discovery → built-in bootstrap/generation → export → deterministic controls → accounting, HF archival and owned cleanup. Codex is not in the execution loop. Main is unchanged; no merge or release.

**Decisive fresh result:** #66 completed the full workflow without per-task repairs: one NiBabel export, nop **0** / oracle **1**, target **0/9 → 9/9**, all **37 P2P tests pass on both sides**, oracle exit **0**. All four HF readbacks, owned cleanup and installed completed replay are verified. This covers the selected test-file command, not every NiBabel test or population yield. [Evidence](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/0d7344963b050bf3743de14d4d6858039c2c6201/experiments/66-fresh-nibabel/results.md). #65’s DendroPy pair is tracked-positive but remains strict-ineligible because four unrelated failures persist. Earlier negatives are preserved.

Import provenance (#56), argument/parser limits (#59), compiled rebuilding (#60) and subtest identities (#64) remain separate, undeployed research. Detailed conclusions, modification rationale and receipts are linked in comments.

**Final accounting:** **$2.196603 / 61 original model calls**, **14.892111111/32 allocated CPUh**; all admitted jobs terminal, CPU/model reservations zero, paid execution disabled. title: Research: assess pr_runtime test selection and parser coverage
body:
How much `pr_runtime` validation coverage is lost through test recognition, command selection and output parsing? Follow-up to #28. Investigation remains open.

**Live result:** excluding deleted test paths removes Matchms PR958's missing-file error, but both stages then fail collection because historical code imports missing `chemap`; no task is recovered. PR671 retains its original 1 fail-to-pass and 30 pass-to-pass tests. [Evidence](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/40a80ef0/experiments/32-runner-coverage/target-live-diagnosis.json).

**Candidate coverage:** a default-off literal pytest targeting policy passes selection and package-routing checks. A separate completion gate detects hidden inner pytest errors in native and exported fixture runs. The frozen MACS PR792 comparison confirms a real upstream stage returned outer exit 0 despite pytest collection errors; the gate itself remains untested on that live case. Neither candidate has recovered a biological task. An original SAMtools `make test` log has 523 case-heading occurrences but only 29 names, while the Perl summary counts 1,052 cases and other make components follow; a reliable adapter needs stable identities and a composite C/Perl/shell contract. [MACS evidence](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/d4626f80/experiments/31-historical-builds/macs-native-diagnosis.json) · [SAMtools audit](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/22fe6841/experiments/32-runner-coverage/samtools-native-log-audit.json) · [Candidate checks](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/ae0ef75b/experiments/32-runner-coverage/pytest-completion-protocol.md).

**MNE boundary:** the unchanged 12 bootstrap actions still exited 127. The exact full-suite smoke check timed out at both 300 and 1,200 seconds, advancing from 28% to 61% partial progress. No image, fresh-image check, PR14445 validation or task export followed. The longer-timeout archive and cleanup are verified. [MNE readback](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/706f369f/experiments/32-runner-coverage/mne-longcheck-readback-001.json).

**Status:** three remote jobs used 2.16248 allocated CPU-hours under the 10-hour ceiling, with zero model calls or new capacity. All owned remote resources are removed. Live biological acceptance of the targeting/completion candidates and a SAMtools composite adapter remain open; no production change is promoted. [Accounting](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/706f369f/experiments/32-runner-coverage/mne-campaign-accounting.json). Detailed logs remain in comments.

title: Research: validate compiled environments after historical PR checkout
body:
Can replaying recorded build commands after a historical PR checkout restore a compiled environment without task-specific repairs? Follow-up to #28. Investigation remains open; no pipeline change is promoted.

**Finding:** The opt-in rebuild hook preserves default-off behavior and passes synthetic native/export integration checks. On frozen MACS PR742, the original validator had collection errors and 0 F2P; the rebuilt arm completed both stages and reported 1 F2P/10 P2P. PR792 remained negative because its test patch imports a module added only by that PR. [Candidate checks](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/6c03d407/experiments/31-historical-builds/native-outcome-results.json) · [PR742 native result](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/015c5e2b/experiments/31-historical-builds/macs-742-native-diagnosis.json).

**Task boundary:** A candidate PR742 Harbor task was emitted with the pinned upstream writer from archived inputs; this was not a fresh official generate run. Its ten files stayed unchanged during the 300-second nop/oracle controls, but both scored 0 with `rebuild_incomplete`: pip could not fetch `setuptools>=80.0` during the recorded editable-install rebuild (`Connection refused`). The F2P/P2P tests were never reached. There is no validated task, solver result or benchmark score. [Control diagnosis](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/a78e6e21/experiments/31-historical-builds/macs-742-control-diagnosis.json) · [Results](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/a78e6e21/experiments/31-historical-builds/macs-742-control-results.json).

**Limits and status:** The image was reconstructed from all 16 recorded actions, with smoke/fresh-image timeouts raised from 300 to 1,200 seconds; mutable dependencies can drift. Source inspection now identifies the pinned upstream export guard: task compose maps PyPI hosts to `0.0.0.0`, while the recorded rebuild needs isolated build dependencies. The resource wrapper preserves that guard. A general offline preparation/cache approach is the next comparison; do not disable answer-leakage protection. Eight terminal jobs used 5.480651 allocated CPU-hours, zero model calls and no new capacity; all owned remote resources were removed. Exact historical MACS BSD-3-Clause notices were already retained under #28, correcting the earlier null-metadata license assessment. All eight reviewed execution archives and provenance are now preserved in HF with 31 anonymously downloaded, checksum-verified objects. No failed result was reclassified. [Boundary evidence](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/abe0c069/experiments/33-unattended-validation/pr742-boundary-review.json) · [Archive receipt](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/abe0c069/experiments/33-unattended-validation/macs-evidence-receipt.json). Follow-up coordination: #33. Detailed run records are in comments.

title: Research: remove pr_runtime large-script argument limits
body:
Can a general transport change remove large-script argument failures without changing native validation behavior? Follow-up to #28. **The bounded comparison is complete; this issue remains open for user review. No production change promoted.**

**Result:** the stdin candidate removes the reproduced Linux `E2BIG` error for Matchms PR958's 425,528-byte post-fix script. Successful control PR671 preserves exactly the same native sets under both transports: 1 fail-to-pass and 30 pass-to-pass tests. Earlier real-Docker probes also verified exact delivery of a 1,080,000-byte payload.

**No recovered task for PR958:** both delivered stages collect zero tests because unchanged upstream targeting includes two files deleted by the patch. This separate failure is tracked in #32. No patch reduction, dependency/test repair, parser change or extra model call was used.

**Limits:** the saved recipe was reconstructed, so mutable dependency drift remains; original failed script bytes were not retained. Both transports leave remote commands alive after client timeout; the comparison aborts timed-out arms and removes their containers. Shell diagnostic/introspection differences remain. Native validation is distinct from exports and independent Harbor controls.

**Accounting and retention:** all five attempts are terminal, totaling 0.25515 allocated CPU-hours on existing reserved capacity, zero model calls. Owned containers/images/cache and tools were removed and absence verified. Raw Matchms evidence has verified private local archive readback; the remote archive has a seven-day TTL.

[Live diagnosis](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/4862b97e/experiments/30-script-transport/live-diagnosis.json) · [Verified archive and cleanup](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/4862b97e/experiments/30-script-transport/live-readback.json) · [Findings and limitations](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/4862b97e/experiments/30-script-transport/findings.md) · [Scope](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/4862b97e/experiments/30-script-transport/issue-scope.md). title: Research: measure pr_runtime losses from timeouts and scheduling
body:
